brief_summary: Three-panel horizontal timeline showing the two compaction moves the article traces: full-size to tenkeyless (numpad removed, function row/nav/arrows retained) and tenkeyless to 60% (function row, nav cluster, and arrow cluster all additionally removed, leaving only alpha block and modifiers). Bronze arrows label each subtraction.
data_sources: 60-percent-layout-history.mdx § 'The first cut: full-size to tenkeyless' — 'A full-size board carries roughly 104–105 keys... The first widely adopted cut removed exactly one of those blocks — the numpad — and nothing else... Function row, nav cluster, and arrows all survived the cut.'

60-percent-layout-history.mdx § 'The first cut: full-size to tenkeyless' — 'TKL was one subtraction: the numpad. 60% is a second, much larger subtraction made a generation later, by a different community, for a different reason.'
